To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the diversity of rodents in the desert of the southwestern United States is highest where rainfall is intermediate, and that the number of species is correlated with rainfall variability.

(a) species diversity in desert rodents increases over a gradient of increasing precipitation; and (b) this pattern is similar to that predicted by Tilmans model for interspecific competition between plants, and is probably caused by the same mechanism.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of productivity on diversity in the desert ecosystem.
the diversity of rodents in arid regions, and the relationship between productivity and diversity.
the effects of productivity on the number of species in a community, and the effects of species number on community structure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the diversity pattern in desert rodent assemblages is caused by a combination of the two mechanisms: (1) a decline in the number of species that can co-exist on a limited resource (productivity), and (2) a decline in disturbance frequency.
Tilman's model applies to animals as well as to plants.
the diversity pattern in rodents is consistent with the predictions of the Tilman model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
diversity in rodents, as in plants, is determined by the productivity of the habitat.
productivity and disturbance are important in determining diversity in the desert.
productivity, in this case rainfall, is the major factor controlling species diversity in the desert.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the productivity–diversitivity relationship may be general.
the diversity-productivity relationship in plants and animals is not just a matter of resource availability, but also of the availability of microhabitats.
the diversity of rodents in the desert is highest at intermediate levels of productivity, as predicted by Tilman.
